The subtitle feature uses large model translation technology to convert human voice in your live stream audio into multilingual content, effectively enhancing the audience's viewing experience in cross\-language, noisy, or silent environments, and helping your content reach a broader global audience. This topic describes how to add a subtitle configuration through the BytePlus MediaLive console.

## Scenarios

* **Barrier\-free viewing**

   Generate source subtitles for hearing\-impaired viewers, supporting barrier\-free viewing experiences in silent places such as offices and libraries, as well as noisy environments like subways and shopping malls.

* **Cross\-border business and global communication**

   Applicable to various scenarios such as cross\-border e\-commerce livestreams, product launches, international conferences, educational training, and speeches by non\-native speakers, facilitating cross\-language communication and market expansion.

## Notes

* **Live latency**: To ensure stable and complete subtitles, an additional **15 to 30 seconds** of live latency will be introduced to associated transcoded streams or ABR substreams, or the source stream with the added subtitle suffix.

* **Billing**

   * **Subtitle**: Billed based on **actual stream push duration**. For more information, see [Subtitle](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-billing-subtitle).

   * **Transcoding**: If you pull a transcoded stream or ABR substream, transcoding fees will be incurred. Billed based on **actual transcoding duration**. The billing time depends on the **Trigger transcoding** setting. For more information, see [Transcoding](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-transcoding).

      * **Stream pulling**: Billing starts when the audience starts pulling the transcoded stream or ABR substream and ends when the transcoding task is complete. Usually less than or equal to the stream push duration.

      * **Stream pushing**: Billing starts when stream pushing begins and ends when stream pushing stops.

* **Activation time**: After adding, updating, or deleting a subtitle configuration, you must wait 3\-5 minutes and then restart pushing your stream for the changed configuration to take effect.

## How it works

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

1. **Configuration and association**: Add a subtitle configuration and associate with one or more live streams using `AppName`, subtitle suffix, and transcoded stream or ABR substream suffix.

2. **Stream pushing and recognition**: After you start pushing the stream, the system will automatically recognize human voice.

3. **Processing and synthesis**: Based on the subtitle configuration, the system processes the recognized human voice, including generating subtitles, generating dubbed audio to replace the original sound, synchronizing the speaker's lip movements with the dubbed audio, and merging the final processed results into the live stream.

4. **Stream pulling**: The audience can watch the final effect by pulling the transcoded stream or ABR substream associated with the subtitle configuration, or the source stream with the added subtitle suffix.

## Prerequisites

* You have added domain names for stream pushing and pulling under the same domain name space. For more information, see [Adding a domain name](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-domain).

* You have added a transcoding or adaptive bitrate (ABR) configuration under the domain name space for subsequent association. Ensure that the transcoding or ABR configuration and subtitle configuration to be added have the same domain name space and `AppName`. For more information, see [Managing transcoding configuration](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-configuring-transcoding) and [Managing adaptive bitrate configuration](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-configuring-an-hls-abr-task).

## Procedure

1. Log in to the [BytePlus MediaLive console](https://console.byteplus.com/live).

2. In the left\-side navigation pane, select **Feature configuration** and click the **Subtitle** tab on the right.

3. In the **Domain name space** drop\-down list, select the domain name space where the transcoding or ABR configuration belongs.

4. Click **Add configuration**.

   ![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/b22b1127bc9c469da772bd6f6521076b~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-topic.webp)

5. In the **Add subtitle configuration** dialog box that appears, complete the following configuration.

   1. Associate the transcoding or ABR configuration.

      |Configuration item |Description |
      |---|---|
      |AppName |The `AppName` of the push stream address. For example, if the push stream address is `rtmp://push.example.com/live/test?authinfo`, then `AppName` is `live`.<br><br>> **Warning**<br><br><br>> Use the same `AppName` as that of the transcoding or ABR configuration.<br> |
      |Subtitle suffix |The subtitle suffix for the source stream. If not configured, the default value is `_subtitle`. You can append this suffix to the source stream address to directly add subtitles, dubbed audio, or lip sync to your source stream, without changing resolution, bitrate, and so on.<br><br>If you need to customize the subtitle suffix, the suffix must start with a hyphen (\-) or underscore (_), be 1–100 characters in length, and support the following characters:<br><br><br>* Uppercase letters A–Z<br><br>* Lowercase letters a–z<br><br>* Hyphen (\-)<br><br>* Underscore (_)<br><br><br>Example:<br><br><br>* Source stream address: `rtmp://pull.example.com/live/test`<br><br>* Subtitle stream (source stream containing subtitles, dubbed audio, or lip sync) address: `rtmp://pull.example.com/live/test_subtitle` |
      |Suffix |Select one or more transcoded stream or ABR substream suffixes (such as `_uhd` and `_hd`) under the current `AppName` to add subtitles, dubbed audio, or lip sync to the transcoded stream or ABR substream. This way, the audience can experience subtitles, dubbed audio, or lip sync when switching quality levels.<br><br>> **Warning**<br><br><br>> Each transcoded stream or ABR substream suffix under an`AppName` can only be bound to one subtitle configuration.<br><br><br>Example:<br><br><br>* Source stream address: `rtmp://pull.example.com/live/test`<br><br>* Transcoded stream or ABR substream (containing subtitles, dubbed audio, or lip sync) address: `rtmp://pull.example.com/live/test_hd` |

   2. Select the appropriate mode based on your scenario.

      |Scenario |Recommended features |Mode selection |Description |
      |---|---|---|---|
      |Provide basic subtitles for the live stream, making it convenient to watch in muted or noisy environments. |Original ASR subtitles |**AI Dubbing** \> **Original (ASR) Subtitles** |Overlay source subtitles over the video using speech recognition. |
      |Enable cross\-language text communication to reach a global audience. |Subtitle translation |**Subtitle Only** or **AI Dubbing** \> **Simultaneous interpretation**<br><br>> **Note**<br><br><br>> We recommend that you select **AI Dubbing** \> **Simultaneous interpretation** for better translation results.<br> |Overlay translated subtitles over the video using speech recognition, while retaining the original sound. |
      |Provide a dubbing\-style translation experience, similar to watching a dubbed film. |Dubbed audio |**AI Dubbing** \> **Simultaneous interpretation** |Provide dubbed audio and replace the original sound. |
      |Pursue an immersive human interpreter experience to enhance professionalism. |Dubbed audio + lip sync |**AI Dubbing** \> **Simultaneous interpretation** |Based on dubbed audio, AI technology synchronizes the speaker's lip movements with the dubbed audio, creating a highly realistic effect. |

   3. Complete the configurations.

      * Simultaneous interpretation

         ![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/5aac202da69547daaef566a4d0c4ed21~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-topic.webp)

         |Configuration item |Description |
         |---|---|
         |Processing Delay |The delay time for translation to complete. The value range is 5–60 seconds. Recommended values are as follows.<br><br><br>* For lip sync, dubbed audio, and subtitles: 20<br><br>* For dubbed audio and subtitles: 12<br><br>* For subtitles only: 8<br><br><br>> **Note**<br><br><br>> If the subtitles appear earlier than the video or original sound, reduce the delay time as needed to align the subtitles with the video or original sound, and vice versa.<br> |
         |Subtitles/Simultaneous Interpretation |Select **Simultaneous interpretation**. |
         |Subtitle Language |Select the source and target languages. The source language supports Chinese and English. The target language supports Chinese, English, Japanese, Spanish, Indonesian, Portuguese, French, and German.<br><br>> **Note**<br><br><br>> The source and target languages must be different.<br> |
         |Write SEI |Whether to write subtitles into SEI messages in the live stream. When enabled, the player can receive the subtitles from the SEI messages.<br><br>> **Note**<br><br><br>> MediaLive uses `100` as the SEI `type` value when writing subtitles into SEI messages. If your stream pushing tool or app also writes custom SEI messages into the stream, avoid using the same SEI `type` value. Otherwise, the player may identify the custom data as subtitles.<br> |
         |Lip Sync |Whether to enable the lip sync feature. Once enabled, the speaker's lip movements will synchronize with the dubbed audio, making the live stream more immersive.<br><br>> **Note**<br><br><br>> After enabling the lip sync feature, the dubbed audio feature will be enabled automatically.<br> |
         |Dubbed Audio |Whether to enable the dubbed audio feature.<br><br>After enabling the feature, the original sound will be replaced by dubbed audio featuring voice cloning effects. You can also do the following:<br><br><br>* **Noise Reduction**: When enabled, the background noise such as electrical noise and environmental noise in dubbed audio is effectively reduced, improving the clarity of the final output audio.<br><br>   > **Warning**<br>   <br><br>   > Enabling noise reduction may cause background sound to disappear.<br>   <br><br>* **Volume Balance**: When enabled, the system automatically adjusts the output audio volume to maintain a stable and comfortable level, effectively preventing sudden changes in volume or harsh explosive sounds, and significantly enhancing the audience's listening experience. |
         |Subtitle |Whether to enable the subtitle feature. When enabled, subtitles will be displayed on the video.<br><br>You can configure the number of display lines, subtitle order (source subtitles on top or bottom), margin, font size, style, base color, and more for source and translated subtitles. For example,<br><br><br>* **Subtitle format**: Set which subtitles are displayed.<br><br>   * **Original + Translation**: Display bilingual subtitles. The display order of subtitles is determined by **Subtitle sorting**.<br><br>   * **Translation**: Only display translated subtitles.<br><br>   * **Original**: Only display source subtitles.<br><br>* **Lines of subtitles**: Set the maximum number of lines displayed for the subtitles in each language.<br><br>   > **Note**<br>   <br><br>   > When displaying bilingual subtitles, this configuration applies to both the source and translated subtitles. For example, if **2 lines** is selected, both the source and translated subtitles will display up to 2 lines each, so the subtitles will occupy a total of 4 lines of screen space.<br>   <br><br>   * **1 line**: Each language's subtitles display up to one line. Content may be truncated.<br><br>   * **2 lines**: Each language's subtitles display up to two lines. Content may be truncated.<br><br>   * **Automatic**: Automatically wraps lines based on the total number of subtitle characters and the maximum number of characters per line to ensure complete content display.<br><br>* **Word count**: The maximum number of characters per line. When **Lines of subtitles** is set to **1 line** or **2 lines**, and the total number of characters in the source or translated subtitles exceeds the display range, the content will be truncated. For example, if the maximum number of characters per line for translated subtitles is 10, **Lines of subtitles** is set to **2 lines**, and the total number of characters in the translated subtitles exceeds 20, any content after the 20th character will be truncated.<br><br>   > **Note**<br>   <br><br>   * > The system calculates the maximum number of characters that can be displayed per line based on factors such as the **Word count**, **Left & right margins**, **Font** **Size**, and screen resolution you configured.<br>   <br><br>   * > Each character, letter, symbol, or digit counts as one character.<br>    |
         |Glossary |Add proprietary vocabulary and expected translations, such as brand names, personal names, product names, or feature names. The system uses the glossary as a reference for the translation model to improve the translation accuracy of proprietary vocabulary, **but the expected translations may not be used every time**. If mistranslations persist after you configure the glossary, add possible mistranslations and their correct translations in **Corrections** to forcibly correct translated subtitles.<br><br>Use the format `original text:translation`, and separate multiple entries with English commas (,). For example, `赛事直播:sports live streaming,实时字幕:real-time subtitles`.<br><br>> **Warning**<br><br><br><br>* > This configuration applies only to **translated subtitles**.<br><br><br>* > In each `original text:translation` entry, the original text and translation cannot contain English commas (,).<br><br><br>* > The total number of characters in the **Glossary** text box cannot exceed 30,000.<br> |
         |Corrections |Configure translated subtitles that need to be forcibly corrected. Add possible mistranslations and their correct translations one by one. Each mistranslation or correct translation must be 1 to 50 characters long. You can add up to 60 corrections. We recommend that you adjust them based on actual results.<br><br>When the system matches a mistranslation, it forcibly replaces the mistranslation with the correct translation. **Corrections modify only translated subtitles and do not modify source subtitles or dubbed audio**. For example, if **LiveCore** is mistranslated as **核心直播**, you can add the following correction: 核心直播 (**Translation**) \> LiveCore (**Correct**).<br><br>> **Warning**<br><br><br>> Corrections match text only and do not determine the context. Use corrections only when the configured text can be clearly identified as incorrect. The correct translation cannot contain the corresponding mistranslation. For example, if you configure **stream** \> **live stream**, and the subtitle already correctly displays **live stream**, the system still replaces **stream** with **live stream**, resulting in **live live stream**.<br> |
         |Callback address |The URL used to receive callback messages. The URL must start with `http://` or `https://`, be publicly accessible, and contain 1–100 characters. For more information about AI Dubbing callback messages, see [AI Dubbing](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-callback-description#ai-dubbing). |

Recommended values are as follows.<br><br><br>* When **Writing Method** is **Whole Sentence**: 15<br><br>* When **Writing Method** is **Live Streaming**: 2\-3<br><br><br>> **Note**<br><br><br>> If the subtitles appear earlier than the video or original sound, reduce the delay time as needed to align the subtitles with the video or original sound, and vice versa.<br> |

When enabled, the player can receive the subtitles from the SEI messages.<br><br>> **Note**<br><br><br><br>* > This field is displayed only when **Writing Method** is set to **Whole Sentence**.<br><br><br>* > MediaLive uses `100` as the SEI `type` value when writing subtitles into SEI messages. For example,<br><br><br>* **Writing Method**: The display mode of source subtitles.<br><br>   * **Whole Sentence**: The subtitles will be displayed one complete sentence at a time. The system waits until a sentence is finished, then displays the entire subtitles corresponding to the audio segment all at once. This method ensures contextual completeness and reading continuity, providing an experience similar to watching movie subtitles.<br><br>   * **Live Streaming**: Subtitles are displayed character by character or word by word, without waiting for the sentence to finish. This method prioritizes real\-time performance, allowing the audience to see the text almost simultaneously with the audio, similar to voice input on a mobile phone.<br><br>* **Original word count**: The maximum number of characters per line.<br><br>   > **Note**<br>   <br><br>   * > The system calculates the maximum number of characters that can be displayed per line based on factors such as the **Original word count**, **Left & right margins**, **Font** **Size**, and screen resolution you configured.<br>   <br><br>   * > Each character, letter, symbol, or digit counts as one character.<br>    |
         |Hot word bank |Add hotwords, such as product names or popular phrases, as a reference for the speech recognition model to improve recognition accuracy. **Hotwords may not be recognized accurately every time**. Hotwords must match the source language, be separated by spaces, and the total number of characters in the **Hot word bank** text box cannot exceed 30,000. If recognition errors persist after you configure hotwords, add possible recognition errors and their corrected forms in **Corrections** to forcibly correct original ASR subtitles. |

Each recognition error or corrected form must be 1 to 50 characters long. You can add up to 60 corrections. We recommend that you adjust them based on actual results.<br><br>When the system matches a recognition error, it forcibly replaces the recognition error with the corrected form. For example, if **MediaLive** is incorrectly recognized as **media life**, you can add the following correction: media life (**Subtitle**) \> MediaLive (**Correct**).<br><br>> **Warning**<br><br><br>> Corrections match text only and do not determine the context. Use corrections only when the configured text can be clearly identified as incorrect. The corrected form cannot contain the corresponding recognition error. For example, if you configure **stream** \> **live stream**, and the subtitle already correctly displays **live stream**, the system still replaces **stream** with **live stream**, resulting in **live live stream**.<br> |

For more information about AI Dubbing callback messages, see [AI Dubbing](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-callback-description#ai-dubbing). |

6. On the right of the dialog box, test the subtitle effects online according to the UI prompts.

   > **Note**

   * > The source stream size selected here is used only for preview and will not change the source stream's resolution. The orientation of the output stream for the task is inherited from the source stream.

   * > There are no restrictions on the size, format, or other attributes of the background image uploaded here.

7. After you confirm that the settings are correct, click **Confirm**. After adding the subtitle configuration, you can edit or delete the subtitle configuration at any time. When editing the configuration, you can modify all configurations except `AppName` and the subtitle suffix.

   After adding, updating, or deleting a subtitle configuration, you must wait 3–5 minutes and restart pushing the stream for the changed subtitle configuration to take effect.

## What to do next

1. Generate the source stream address, transcoded stream address or ABR address using the [address generator](https://console.byteplus.com/live/main/locationGenerate).

   1. Complete the following configurations, and click **Generates Pull stream address**.

      * **Address type**: Select **Pull stream address**.

      * **Domain name**: Select the domain name for stream pulling within the domain name space used when adding the subtitle configuration.

      * **AppName** and **StreamName**: Enter the `AppName` and `StreamName` from your push stream address. For example, if the push stream address is `rtmp://push.example.com/live/test?authinfo`, then the `AppName` is `live`, and the `StreamName` is `test`.

   2. Get the source stream address, transcoded stream address or ABR address.

      ![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/08bc95d5a1b144a793498b0d1e744849~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-topic.webp)

      * Source stream address: Manually append the subtitle suffix to the obtained source stream address. For example, if the source stream address is `rtmp://pull.example.com/live/test` and the subtitle suffix is `_subtitle`, you must use `rtmp://pull.example.com/live/test_subtitle` to play the source stream that includes subtitles, dubbed audio, or lip sync.

      * Transcoded stream address or ABR address: Use the obtained transcoded stream address or ABR address to play the transcoded stream or ABR substream that includes subtitles, dubbed audio, or lip sync.

2. Use your push stream address to push the source stream, and the subtitle task will start automatically. Ensure that the live content includes clear, stable human voice audio.

3. Use any of the following methods to pull the transcoded stream or ABR substream associated with the subtitle configuration, or the source stream with the added subtitle suffix, to experience subtitles, dubbed audio, or lip sync.

   |Method |Scenario |Description |
   |---|---|---|
   |Third\-party stream pulling tool |No SDK development resources. |Configure the pull stream address in the third\-party stream pulling tool to play the live stream. For more information, refer to the corresponding official documentation or consult official customer support. |
   |Player SDK for Web |Watch the live stream in a web browser. |Integrate the Player SDK for Web and play the live stream on your website or web app. For more information, see [Integrating the Player SDK for Web](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-integrating-the-player-sdk-for-web_1). |
   |Client SDK |Watch the live stream in your own mobile app. |Integrate the client SDK and play the live stream in a mobile app. For more information, see:<br><br><br>* iOS: [Integrating the Player SDK for iOS](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-integrating-the-broadcast-and-player-sdks-for-ios)<br><br>* Android: [Integrating the Player SDK for Android](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-integrating-the-broadcast-and-player-sdks-for-android)<br><br>* Flutter: [Integrating the Player SDK for Flutter](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/integrating-the-player-sdk-for-flutter)<br><br>* React Native: [Integrating the Player SDK for React Native](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-integrating-the-broadcast-and-player-sdks-for-rn) |
   |BytePlus MediaLive console |For quick preview and debugging during development or testing. |On the [Web pull page](https://console.byteplus.com/live/main/webPullStream/play) in the console, enter the pull stream address to quickly verify playback. For more information, see [Pulling a stream through the console](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/docs-web-pull).<br><br>> **Note**<br><br><br>> Only supports playing FLV, HLS, and RTM streams.<br> |

## FAQ

### Why can't I see the subtitles or is the subtitle configuration not taking effect?

If you have added the subtitle configuration but cannot see the subtitles or the subtitle configuration is not taking effect, please check the following issues one by one:

* **Check the activation time**: There is a **3\-5 minute** delay for the subtitle configuration to take effect. Please ensure you have waited long enough after completing the configuration.

* **Check whether you have restarted pushing the stream**: After adding or updating the subtitle configuration, you must **stop and restart pushing the stream** to load the new configuration. Please confirm that you have performed this operation.

* **Check the source stream**: Ensure that the live content includes **clear, stable human voice audio**. If the live content is silent or the background sound is too loud, the system will not be able to recognize the audio and therefore cannot generate subtitles.

* **Check whether the subtitle feature is enabled**: If you select the **AI Dubbing** mode, ensure that the **Subtitle** switch is turned on.

   ![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/6a66b44ee3094a2eb7d36328e3502652~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-topic.webp)

* **Check whether the dubbed audio feature is enabled**: Only after the dubbed audio feature is enabled will dubbed audio be provided. Otherwise, only the original sound will be output.

   ![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/8ce3a18afd364c5fab9986b7728dedf9~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-topic.webp)

* **Check the pull stream address**: Ensure that you are using the correct pull stream address. The pull stream address must be the transcoded stream address or ABR address associated with the subtitle configuration, or the source stream address with the subtitle suffix added.

* **Check the source and target language configuration**: Ensure that the source language matches the language in the source stream audio, and that the target language is the one required by the audience.

### Why can't I select a transcoded stream or ABR substream suffix?

![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/4da95dbffa0d4f908786402adf2945c2~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-topic.webp)

Make sure that the `AppName` you enter in the subtitle configuration is the same as the `AppName` of the transcoding or ABR configuration you want to associate.

### My live stream is aimed at a global audience. How can I provide subtitles in different languages for them?

Add subtitle configurations for multiple target languages under the same `AppName`. When you use this `AppName` to push the stream, the audience can select the subtitle language as needed.

In the following example, when you push the stream with `AppName` **live**, the audience can switch between English subtitles, Japanese subtitles, and a version without subtitles. Additionally, for each subtitle version, they can switch between original, Ultra\-High Definition (UHD), and High Definition (HD) quality levels.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

1. On the [transcoding configuration](https://console.byteplus.com/live/main/application/transcode?vhostParam=autostabletest.live.videoarchserverqa.xyz) or [ABR configuration](https://console.byteplus.com/live/main/application/abr?vhostParam=autostabletest.live.videoarchserverqa.xyz) page, add the following suffix configurations for `AppName` **live**:

   * `_uhd` (UHD quality level without subtitles)

   * `_hd` (HD quality level without subtitles)

   * `_enuhd` (UHD quality level with English subtitles)

   * `_enhd` (HD quality level with English subtitles)

   * `_jpuhd` (UHD quality level with Japanese subtitles)

   * `_jphd` (HD quality level with Japanese subtitles)

2. On the [subtitle configuration](https://console.byteplus.com/live/main/application/subtitleManagement?vhostParam=autostabletest.live.videoarchserverqa.xyz) page, add the following subtitle configurations for `AppName` **live**:

   * Set the subtitle suffix to `_en`, associate with the transcoded stream or ABR substream suffixes `_enuhd` and `_enhd`, and set the target language to English.

   * Set the subtitle suffix to `_jp`, associate with the transcoded stream or ABR substream suffixes `_jpuhd` and `_jphd`, and set the target language to Japanese.

3. Use the push stream address `rtmp://push.example.com/live/test` to push the source stream.

4. The audience can switch between different languages and quality levels by using different pull stream addresses.

### For a live stream where only subtitles in specific languages are needed and I do not want to enable all subtitles, what should I do?

By default, after configuring subtitles in multiple languages for an `AppName`, when you use this `AppName` to push the stream, the system will automatically start all associated subtitle tasks. This may result in unnecessary costs in scenarios where only subtitles in certain languages are required.

To resolve this issue, you can add the following parameters to the push stream address to precisely control which subtitle languages are enabled for each stream pushing.

* `custom_trans`: This parameter must be included and set the value to `1` for the system to recognize the `trans_suffix` parameter. If this parameter is not included, the system will, by default, start all associated subtitle tasks.

* `trans_suffix`: Specifies the subtitle suffix, transcoded stream suffix, or ABR substream suffix to start the subtitle task for this stream pushing. Separate parameter values with an English comma (`,`). For example, if the push stream address is `rtmp://push.example.com/live/test`, you have configured English subtitles for the subtitle suffix `_en` and French subtitles for the transcoded stream suffix `_fr`. You can use the following push stream address to enable only English and French subtitles: `rtmp://push.example.com/live/test?custom_trans=1&trans_suffix=_en,_fr`.

> **Warning**

> If a live stream does not require any subtitles to be displayed, simply add `custom_trans=1` to the push stream address, for example, `rtmp://push.example.com/live/test?custom_trans=1`. In this case, subtitle fees will not be charged.

### Which should I choose: the AI Dubbing task or the AI Dubbing mode of subtitle configuration?

The AI Dubbing task and the AI Dubbing mode of subtitle configuration use the same translation model and deliver identical translation results. Please select the appropriate mode based on your specific scenario.

* If the following scenarios apply, we recommend that you choose the AI Dubbing task. For more information, see [Creating an AI Dubbing task](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-media-live/ai-liveinterpret-simultaneous-audio-and-video-interpretation#0946c25d).

   * **Event\-oriented**: Translation is needed for a single or a few important events, such as product launches or international conferences.

   * **Manual control required**: You want to enable translation only during specific periods in the live stream, such as when non\-native speakers are speaking.

   * **Low latency required**: For live streaming scenarios with high demands for low latency, such as sports events, you can choose the **Real\-Time Interpretation** mode to reduce latency.

* If you have a large number of live rooms that require translation to be enabled regularly and automatically, we recommend that you choose the AI Dubbing mode of subtitle configuration.

### My live stream only has subtitles but no audio. Can I use the subtitle feature?

No, you cannot. The subtitle feature only supports recognizing and translating human voice content, but cannot translate based on source subtitles.

### Can I export subtitle files?

No, you cannot. BytePlus MediaLive currently does not support exporting subtitle files.

### My live stream involves multiple languages. For example, the host speaks Chinese, but sings Japanese songs during the live stream. Can all of this be translated into English?

No, this is not supported. Currently, automatic detection of the live stream language is not supported. Translation only works between the source and target languages configured in the task. In such cases, we recommend that you set the source language to the host’s primary language, such as Chinese. In this example, only the Chinese content will be translated into English, while the Japanese songs will remain untranslated.
